17_marg1680: AND SOLOMON DETERMINED etc. BEDE. The house which Solomon built in Jerusalem signifies the universal Church, because from the first elect to the last it is built daily through the grace of the true peacemaker; which is still partly a pilgrim in the world, partly, having escaped its toils, already reigns with him in heaven, where it is all to reign when the judgment is finished. To this house belong the angels, likeness to whom is promised us, the Lord saying: "For they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God" etc. To it belongs Christ himself, who says: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. But he spoke of the temple of his body." Of us the Apostle says: "Know you not that you are the temple of God?" etc. If then he, by the humility he took on, was made the temple of God, and we by his Spirit dwelling in us, it is plain that that temple was a figure of all of us and of Christ himself: but of him as of the cornerstone, of us as of living stones built upon him. The tabernacle made in the desert designates the same house of God. But because that house [was made] on the journey by which they were coming to the land of promise, while this was built in the land of promise and in the city of Jerusalem; that, so that, carried from place to place by the Levites, it might at length be brought into the land of promise; this, so that, built at once in the homeland and the royal city, it might stand on an immovable foundation until it should fulfil the very reality of the heavenly figures: in that can be figured the labour and exile of the present Church, in this the future rest and blessedness. Or because that was made by the children of Israel alone, but this by proselytes and gentiles also, in that can be figured chiefly the fathers of the old Testament and the ancient people of God, in this the Church gathered from the gentiles; although the building of each house, taken in particular, shows by manifold figures both the daily labours of the Church and the future joys of the heavenly kingdom, and the election of the first Church from Israel and the salvation of all nations in Christ. And that Solomon is said to have determined to build a house to the name of the Lord and a palace for himself signifies the same thing, because the Church is both the house of God, which he inhabits for ever, and the palace of the heavenly king, in which he shows the greatness of his glory to all generations. The workmen of Solomon are all the elect who prepare themselves for the building of God by believing, working, and teaching others.
17_marg1681: Both by name and by his most peaceful reign he signifies him of whom Isaias says: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace." And Hiram, which is interpreted 'living on high', [signifies] the believers from the gentiles, glorious in life and faith, by whose work the Church is often helped and increased, and strengthened by imperial decrees against heretics, schismatics and pagans. Solomon, then, asks help of Hiram in the work of the temple, because Christ, wishing to build the Church, chose workmen not only from the Jews but also from the gentiles. Hiram sent to Solomon cedar and fir wood cut from Libanus, to be set in the house of the Lord; because the converted gentile world sent to the Lord men renowned in the world, but cast down and humbled from the mountain of pride by the axe of the Lord's rebuke, to be set at some time, in their measure, according to the rule of gospel truth. He sent also craftsmen to be set over the ruling of peoples, namely Dionysius the Areopagite, Cyprian, and many others. He sent also gold, that is, wise men, renowned also in genius. For all these, the gentile world, having given them, awaits from the Lord the gifts of heavenly grace: the wheat, that is, of the word of God, and the oil of charity, of the anointing and enlightening of the Holy Spirit.

17_marg1682: My apostles and first teachers, who form and instruct the teachers from the gentiles, lest they presume to teach anything wrong. 17_marg1684: WHO KNEW HOW TO WORK IN GOLD, SILVER, BRASS, IRON etc. In all these the spiritual Hiram knows how to work, so that the adornment of the house of God may shine with worthy beauty before the eyes of men, and be made acceptable to God by the odour of good repute.
17_marg1685: AND WE WILL CUT etc. It signifies that the gentile world, having heard the fame of the gospel, sends divers persons through faith to baptism. Yet it belongs to the true peacemaker alone to unite them to the unity of the Church by absolving their sins through the sacraments of baptism; of whom it is said: "He upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining upon him, he it is that baptizeth."

17_marg1686: The workmen of the house of the Lord were of the children of Israel, of the proselytes, [and] of the gentiles: of the children of Israel, thirty thousand, who were sent to cut cedars from Libanus, as we read in Kings; of the proselytes, of whom namely he now speaks, the hewers of stones; of the gentiles, Hiram himself and his servants, who cut wood from Libanus with the servants of Solomon. 17_marg1688: The Church is signified by the threshingfloor. Whence: "Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor." Ornan, that is, 'adornment', a Jebusite by nation, signifies the gentiles, who are to be adorned by the Lord and changed into sons of the Church. Whence: "You were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord." Jebus is Jerusalem itself. Jebus is interpreted 'trodden down', Jerusalem 'vision of peace'; while the gentile Ornan reigned in it, it was called Jebus. But when David bought in it the place of the holocaust, and when Solomon built the temple, it was called Jerusalem. 17_marg1689: That is, May, namely soon after the Pasch, so that the people, consecrated by the mystical solemnity, might worthily undertake the mystical work.
17_marg1690: After the fulfilment of the dispensation of the divine incarnation, which is written in the four gospels, the Spirit being sent from heaven, the Church was built. What we have expounded in the books of Kings we touch on briefly in Paralipomenon.
17_marg1691: The length of the house signifies the long patience of the Church; the breadth, the charity by which it loves even its enemies, until it rejoices in God with friends alone; the height, the hope of the future life and reward, because it despises all adversities until it sees the good things of the Lord in the land of the living. It is to be noted that the thirty cubits of height which are read in Kings reached not to the roof of the temple but to the lower upper chamber. For here [it is said] that the height was a hundred and twenty cubits [unclear in the edition: "Hic enim quod"]. Another thirty will be counted to the middle chamber, another to the third, then another thirty up to the topmost roof of the temple; and so the whole height of the house is completed in a hundred and twenty cubits, the number of men with which the primitive Church in Jerusalem received the grace of the Holy Spirit. For fifteen, which is made up of seven and eight, signifies the future life, which is now passed in the rest of souls and will be perfected in the resurrection of bodies; and fifteen drawn into a triangle, that is, numbered with all its parts, makes a hundred and twenty, by which the future blessedness of the elect is designated. And well is the third chamber of the house completed in this number, [blessedness] which, after the present labours, after the rest of souls, will be fulfilled in the resurrection in the full glory of happiness.
17_marg1692: That is, the temple itself, which was before the doors of the oracle. For the structure had a threefold division: the porch before the temple; the temple itself, in which were the altar of incense, the table of proposition and the candlestick of light; and the oracle, that is, the Holy of holies, where the ark of the testament and the cherubim were placed behind the veil. The porch before the temple bears the figure of the faithful of old; the temple itself, of those who came into the world after the Lord's incarnation; and the inner house, of the joys of the heavenly kingdom given to both. It is to be noted, then, that the walls of the house were made of precious stones, covered with boards of cypress or cedar, clothed with plates of gold. Whence in Kings: "And all the house was covered with cedar" etc. The stones of the wall or of the pavement, the boards and the gold signify the life of the saints in the Church. The living stones are the saints joined into one rule by the strength of faith. The boards of cedar or cypress are the saints joined to one another in the same faith by the breadth of various virtues, according to the gift of the Holy Spirit. The plates of gold are the saints who have the charity that surpasses knowledge, and rejoice together in its most pleasing brightness.
17_interl2227: the carving of palm trees [is] the portrayal of the virtues, through which true victory and reward are gained
17_interl2228: the offices of charity, by which the brotherhood of the saints is joined and built into the one house of Christ throughout the world
17_interl2229: in Kings thus: "He covered the floor with planks of fir". Hence it is plain that he laid the boards not on the earth but on marble, and thirdly laid gold upon them
17_marg1693: He paved also the floor etc. As the breadth of the wall, rising on high and reaching to the ceilings, signifies the progress of the virtues by which the saints reach heaven, or the choirs of the saints succeeding one another through various times, so the evenness of the pavement [signifies] their harmonious humility, by which, placed in this life, they live together in social charity. The pavement was laid with precious marble of great beauty, and the marble covered with boards of fir, because the life of the just is first to be fortified in the heart by firmness of faith, afterwards to be adorned in work by the breadth of the virtues. For what does the beauty of marble covered with boards profit, unless it show something mystical? But it signifies that the breadth of good works is to be propped up by the strength of faith. The fir, tall and lasting, shows the mind of the elect, spurning the lowest things, cleaving to heavenly things, and excelling in the virtue of patience. The plates of gold laid upon the marble and the boards of fir are the breadth of charity from a pure heart and a good conscience and an unfeigned faith, which, as gold outshines other metals, so outshines the other virtues in the temple of God.
17_interl2232: Solomon covered the walls of the temple with gold when Christ enlightened the company of the faithful with the light of wisdom and charity
17_marg1694: THE POSTS AND THE DOORS etc. He covered them when, the Lord himself opening the entrance of faith, he showed with what truth it shines for all who enter the Church. The door of the temple is Christ, through whom one comes to the Father, who says: "I am the door" etc. In Kings it is written thus: "The oracle was twenty cubits in length, and twenty in breadth, and twenty in height." The Holy of holies is called the oracle because there secrets are revealed to men by divine and angelic speech. Hence the oracle was made in a hidden place, that is, in the inner house, because in the heavenly homeland the vision and speech of angels and the very presence of God will be revealed. That he says twenty cubits of height signifies the wall of cedar which separates the oracle from the outer house.
17_interl2233: the angelic manner of life in the morals of men, that as he is served by angels in heaven, so he may be served by men on earth
17_marg1695: This house has, as is read in Kings, "carved work standing out", when the saints do the works of virtues not in secret, but set forth an example to all.
17_marg1696: The oracle, where the ark was, had twenty cubits in length, breadth and height, that is, it was square; because in the heavenly homeland, where the saints see the king in his beauty, charity alone, of divine and heavenly grace, shines through all things. Whence in what follows: He covered it with plates of gold, that is, he filled the walls of the heavenly city with the grace of charity.
17_marg1697: In talents [is] the perfection of weight, which expresses the perfection of charity, as [does] the perfection of the six, by which the hundred is multiplied to make six hundred.
17_marg1698: HE MADE ALSO NAILS etc. By the number fifty are figured the remission of sins, spiritual grace and eternal rest; and the nails fastened the plates of gold on the walls of the house of the Lord. The nails are the heavenly words by which we advance and are preserved in the love of good works; these promise us pardon of sins through the grace of the Holy Spirit, and an eternal sabbath rest in the future. These are the nails of love and the nails of fear, by which beginners, not yet come to perfection, mortify the allurements of vices, pierced, that is, by those words of truth by which we are taught to crucify our flesh with its vices and concupiscences. Whence the prophet: "Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear" etc. He who comes to more perfect things says of the nails of perfection: "But it is good for me to adhere to my God." The upper chambers also he overlaid with gold. As the Holy of holies, where the ark was, signifies the inward life of the saints in the sight of the Redeemer, whence: "Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, from the disturbance of men", so the upper chambers on high [signify] that the same life is in heaven and not in this world; whence: "Seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God."
17_interl2234: the two cherubim were of one measure and the same work, because there is no differing will in the heavenly homeland, where all are enlightened by the same vision and glory of God present
17_interl2235: because of the fellowship of charity, which cannot be between fewer than two. Hence the disciples are sent two by two to preach, that those who preach the word of faith may hold charity before all things
17_marg1699: HE MADE ALSO TWO CHERUBIM etc. This is read more fully in Kings, written thus: "And he made in the oracle two cherubims of olive tree, of ten cubits in height. One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits, that is, in all ten cubits, from the extremity of one wing to the extremity of the other wing. And the second cherub was also ten cubits, of equal measure, and the work was one in both the cherubims, that is, one cherub had the height of ten cubits, and in like manner the other cherub. And he set the cherubims in the midst of the inner temple: and the cherubims stretched forth their wings, and the wing of one touched one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall: and the other wings in the midst of the temple touched one another."
17_marg1700: "And he set the cherubims", as is read in Kings, "in the midst of the inner temple: and the cherubims stretched forth their wings, and the wing of one touched one wall" etc. It is manifest from what has been said before that the cherubim, whose dwelling is in heaven, are as it were set in the midst of the inner temple. And they stretched forth their wings as if to fly, because the angels always have a mind ready for the service of the divine will. That one wing touched one wall, and the wing of the second cherub the other wall, belongs to that ministry of charity which the angels show us. That the other wings touched one another in the midst of the temple signifies that grace of love with which they embrace one another. "He overlaid also the cherubims with gold", because the Creator raised their nature with immortal brightness and filled their mind with the light of true love and humility.
17_marg1701: Cherubim is a name of angelic dignity. In the singular it is called cherub, in the plural cherubim. Hence by the cherubim can be understood the angels who in heaven always stand by their Creator. They were made of olive wood, because the angelic powers are anointed with the grace of the Holy Spirit, lest they wither from the love of God. And they are ten cubits high, because they enjoy the denarius of eternal life, having the inviolate image of the Creator, keeping the holiness, justice and truth which they received in their first creation. For the denarius consists of ten obols, and contains in itself the name and image of the king. Hence it signifies the heavenly kingdom, where the angels remain for ever in the image of the Creator to which they were made, and elect men receive the image which they had lost by sinning. Wings, when set down in figure of holy men, signify their virtues, by which they always fly to heavenly things and delight to dwell in them; but when in figure of angels, the grace of their perpetual and unfailing happiness, by which they persist always in heaven in the ministry of their Maker. Or because they are endowed with the lightness of a spiritual nature, so that wherever they will they arrive at once as if flying, both here they are figured with wings, and to the prophets they were shown with wings.
17_marg1702: The two cherubim, that is, the two Testaments, made in the oracle, in the secret counsel of the divine dispensation; of olive wood, because they give us the light of knowledge, the flame of the charity of God helping through the Holy Spirit; ten cubits high, because they preach the keeping of the Decalogue for the service of God, to be rewarded with the denarius of the everlasting kingdom.
17_marg1703: "One wing of the cherub was five cubits" etc., because the angels keep with unwearied devotion the law of God written in five books, namely by loving God with all their strength and their neighbours as themselves: "And love is the fulfilling of the law." And the angelic spirits and elect men are neighbours to one another. Hence each wing of the cherub is of the same measure, because with the same devotion with which they love one another in God they desire also our fellowship as we ascend to them. Likewise then the wings make up ten cubits, when in the twofold showing of charity the angels rejoice in the presence of their Creator.
17_marg1704: They touch the two walls equally with their wings, because they have with them Jews and gentiles as possessors of the heavenly court; not that there is any local distinction there between the two peoples, but because the festival of inward blessedness is greater from the fellowship of the brotherhood united in God. They stretch their wings, then, to both walls, because, rejoicing in the heavenly homeland, they stir the just of both peoples to the praise of the Creator.
17_marg1705: They stretch their wings, overlaid with gold, to the walls of the oracle, as they have their faces turned to the outer house; because the angels, as they keep their own innocence, so rejoice in the blessedness of the saints, that they bring help to those whom they still see on earth, until they bring them into the heavenly homeland: "For they are all ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation."
17_marg1706: With the outer wings this one touches one wall, that one the other; because [unclear in the edition: "Vetus Testamentum antiquo populo scripto novum nobis"], who came to the faith after the Lord's incarnation; and we are rightly compared to the second wall, that is, the northern, who after the cold and darkness of idolatry have known the light of truth.
17_interl2236: the work was one in the two cherubim, because the writers of both Testaments serve God with the same chastity of work and devotion of charity, and preach God with one harmonious voice and faith
17_interl2237: because in all the changeableness of passing things the saints stretch out the senses of their body in obedience to their Creator
17_interl2238: the inner wings touch one another over the ark, because the Testaments agree in equal witness concerning the Lord
17_marg1707: They stretch their wings to one another over the ark when they refer to the praise of the Saviour every good thing they had received. They stretch their other wings to the walls of the oracle when they rejoice to see the saints with them, and touch them as with the tips of their wings, exulting that they were imitators of their purity in this life.
17_interl2239: because they desire us, raised up from the toil of this pilgrimage, to come to their fellowship
17_marg1708: AND THEIR FACES WERE TURNED TOWARD THE OUTWARD HOUSE, because for the sake of us, who still stand outside, but "are saved by hope", the divine books were composed, whose writers, already reigning with the Lord, take care of our salvation and intercede for us with God.
17_interl2241: by the desire of heavenly things, in which we ought to be initiated by carrying our cross
17_interl2242: by the sacrament of the Lord's passion
17_interl2243: by the flame of spiritual love; whence those who walked with the Lord said: "Was not our heart burning" etc.
17_interl2244: by chastening of the flesh; whence: "Mortify your members which are upon the earth"
17_marg1709: This is passed over in Kings, but there is told what is not had here, namely that "in the entrance of the oracle he made little doors of olive tree, and posts". But this veil was made for the sake of beauty, that the silk might shine between the gilded walls. But it is of the same mystery as the little doors, hung with fitting signification before the ark and at the entrance of the oracle, so that, as the little doors were opened at fitting hours, so also the veil [was drawn] for those coming who were to enter the Holy of holies. Its drawing back according to the law signifies the opening of the heavenly kingdom, which is given to us through the flesh of Christ. Hence also when the Lord was baptized the heavens were opened, because through the baptism which he consecrated for us we enter the gate of the heavenly kingdom; and when he died the veil was rent in the midst, because the figures of the law had come to an end, and the truth of the gospel and the entrance of the kingdom are opened by the truth itself.
17_marg1710: The cherubim are woven into these four colours when in all that we do devoutly we are protected by angelic guard from the poisoned darts of the demons, and make unceasing use of the fulness of knowledge, ever looking to the divine words, lest we stray from the path of the virtues.
17_marg1711: They stood in the porch before the doors of the temple, and adorned the entrance of the temple on either side with their beauty. The door of the temple is the Lord, who says: "No man cometh to the Father but by me" etc. The pillars stand round the door on either side when the ministers of the word show the entrance of the heavenly kingdom to both peoples, so that whoever comes to the faith of the gospel from the light of the knowledge of the law or from the error of the gentiles may have them ready to show him the way of salvation by word and example.
17_marg1712: In Kings we read of these pillars: "And when he was come to king Solomon, he wrought all his work. And he cast two pillars in brass" etc.
17_marg1713: This number signifies the perfection of the masters. For the number seven multiplied by five, or five by seven, gives thirty-five. Five expresses the law; seven, because of the sevenfold Spirit abiding on the flower of the root of Jesse, the gospel. Hence the Lord is related in one place to have fed five thousand men with five loaves, and in another four thousand men with seven loaves. The pillars of thirty-five cubits, then, signify that the teachers of the gospel have perfect knowledge of the two Testaments; whence: "To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God." And elsewhere: "He opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures."
17_marg1714: The manifold weaving together of the chains, and the spreading of the net according to Kings, suggest the manifold persons of the elect, who, when they cleave to the words of the preachers by listening faithfully and obeying, offer to beholders the wonder of their joining, as nets and little chains laid upon the heads of the pillars.
17_marg1715: The heads of the pillars, that is, the topmost part, are the hearts of the teachers, by whose thoughts devoted to God all their works and words are directed, as the limbs by the head.
17_marg1716: Many grains within are surrounded by one rind outside; hence they signify the Church, because it surrounds the innumerable hosts of the elect with the defence of one faith; or the life and morals of each just man, who walls in with the firm guard of faith and humility his many marks of thoughts and virtues, lest perhaps they flow away. And fitly were the heads of the pillars surrounded round about with pomegranates, because the holy teachers call to mind the life of the faithful of former times, and confirm their own words on every side by their examples, lest they err, if they live or teach otherwise than their rule holds.
17_interl2245: the right-hand pillar signifies the teachers, because they founded the primitive Church in Jerusalem
17_marg1717: THESE PILLARS ALSO. Two pillars were made, and so placed, to teach us to keep the entrance of the heavenly kingdom before our eyes in prosperity and in adversity. And it is to be noted that the porch of the temple is also called the vestibule, and that what we read, between the vestibule and the altar, ought to be understood as between the porch and the altar.
17_marg1718: The second pillar signifies the preachers who were sent to preach to the gentiles. Or the right-hand pillar signifies those who prophesied that the Lord would come in the flesh; the second, those who testify that he has already come and redeemed the world with his blood. Both pillars are reckoned by a like name, since one is called 'firmness' and the other 'in strength', that one strength of faith and work may be shown to be in all teachers; and the teachers of our time are silently censured, who wish to seem and be called pillars of the house of God, when they have in themselves nothing of the strength of firm faith for despising the pomps of the world [and] desiring invisible goods, [nothing of strength] for correcting, or of diligence for understanding, the errors of those over whom they are set.
17_marg1719: The altar of holocaust signifies those who consecrate their body and soul to God with the fire of love; whose perseverance in good work the length of the altar expresses, the breadth their largeness in the charity of God and neighbour, the height their hope in awaiting [God's] visitation.
17_marg1720: OF TWENTY CUBITS IN BREADTH etc. The twenty signifies the great perfection of unwearied longsuffering and sincere love, which is given us through the keeping of both Testaments. For four fives are twenty; and there are five books of the law and four gospels. And when, grace enlightening, we come to the understanding and keeping of the law, we complete the number twenty; and the same number is in the length and breadth of the altar when the hearts of the elect, both Testaments teaching them, keep perseverance in such work even in persecutions, and cheerfulness of love even toward those who persecute.
17_marg1721: In the ten the hope of heavenly rewards is signified. Hence those who labour in the vineyard of the householder are rewarded with a denarius. Hence the altar, which signifies the elect, is raised ten cubits, to signify their everlasting life.
17_marg1722: A BRAZEN SEA ALSO etc. The saving laver in which we are washed for the remission of sins. For the priests were washed in it, as is said in what follows, who signify all the elect, because they are members of the true priest. And rightly is this vessel called a sea, namely in memory of the Red Sea, in which, the Egyptians being destroyed and the people of God freed, the form of baptism went before. And baptism seeks of us cleanness of life in this world and promises the glory of eternal life in the future. Hence the sea is said to be ten cubits from brim to brim, because all that we ought to do is expressed in ten precepts. By the denarius also is signified the reward of good deeds, when it is promised to those labouring in the vineyard. The sea was therefore ten cubits from brim to brim: from the first baptized in the name of Jesus Christ to the last, the whole choir of the faithful ought to enter the one way of truth and hope from the Lord for the common crown of justice.
17_interl2250: that the whole world might be signified as to be cleansed by the laver of life
17_marg1723: Because whatever we offend by sight, hearing, smell, taste or touch is all loosed in baptism. But the remission of past sins does not suffice unless each one thereafter applies himself to good works. Otherwise the devil who had gone out returns more manifold, and the last state of the man is made worse than the first. Hence he adds: And a line of thirty etc.
17_marg1724: This is the discipline of the heavenly precepts, by which we are bound back from our own wills. Whence: "A threefold cord is not easily broken", because the keeping of God's commandments in the hearts of the saints, made firm by faith, hope and love of the heavenly reward, can be loosed by no adversity.
17_interl2251: These are the twelve apostles and their vicars, who carry the sea laid upon them when with ready devotion they fulfil the office of evangelizing enjoined on them, and build up the faith of the holy Trinity in the parts of the four-square world
17_marg1725: The carving ran round under the brim, encircling the sea for ten cubits. Two rows of storied carvings were cast. Since it was said before that "a line of thirty cubits compassed the sea", and it is now added that the carving placed under the brim encircled it for ten cubits, it is plain that the vessel was spread out and widened in the manner of a bowl, narrowing from the thirty cubits it had at the brim to ten. And storied carving is that which imitates the histories of things. Hence by the storied carvings with which the sea is surrounded the examples of former times are designated, that we may see by what works the saints pleased God from the beginning, and in what great unhappiness the reprobate perished for their crimes.
17_marg1726: THE HINDER PARTS etc. Because with what reward the preachers will be endowed for ever is arranged by the judgment of God, but is still hidden to us, to whom this cannot be hidden: that everyone who receives baptism unto salvation ought to have faith, hope and charity, and without these three virtues can neither work nor enter into salvation. Hence in Kings it is said: "And the thickness of the laver [was] three inches." The thickness of the laver is the firmness of virtue; of three inches, because the receiving of baptism is fortified by the strength of faith, hope and love.
17_marg1727: NOW THE THICKNESS OF IT etc. A thickness which Josephus said was of four fingers, showing what the size of the handbreadth was. And these signify the same thing. For whoever does works in faith, hope and charity according to the teaching of the four gospels receives the reward of justice and of eternal life.
17_interl2252: the taste of the Lord's passion
17_interl2253: the open brightness of the resurrection
17_marg1728: The thousand signifies perfection, because the ten makes a solid square. For ten times ten make a hundred, which is as it were a square figure, but flat; but that it may rise in height and be made solid, multiply a hundred by ten and they make a thousand. By this number the stable, unconquerable and as it were four-square conscience of the just is signified. For whichever way you turn a square, it will stand. So the mind of the elect is bent by no temptation from its state of uprightness.
17_marg1729: The sea holds three thousand measures when the sacrament of baptism, given in the faith of the Trinity, confers on those washed in it the remission of all sins.
17_interl2255: how these lavers were made is written more fully in Kings
17_marg1730: In Kings thus: "He made also ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty bates, and was of four cubits. And upon every base, in all ten, he put as many lavers" etc. The apostles and apostolic men, who are signified by the oxen carrying the sea, are expressed also by the bases prepared for carrying the lavers, as the lavers themselves signify baptism, which the sea figured. For in them the priests washed all that they were to offer in holocausts. And by the holocaust of the Lord can be understood the whole multitude of the faithful, which is baptized by him in water and fire. As then the priests washed in the sea signify those who through baptism are made partners of the high priest, so the holocausts express the same when after the washing of baptism they are filled with spiritual grace. For the victim is washed in the laver when the faithful man is drenched with the water of baptism; it is offered in holocaust when through the laying on of the bishop's hand he receives the gift of the Holy Spirit.
17_marg1731: The bases of the lavers were set on both sides of the temple, so that the grace of the sacred font might be signified as to be opened to both peoples. And there are five on each side, so that, as in the exposition of the sea, which we have said was five cubits high, it might be typically shown that all that had been offended through the five senses of the body was to be remitted through the laver of baptism. As then in the one sea set upon twelve oxen is expressed the unity of baptism, which was to be preached through the apostles in all the world, so also by the two rows of lavers it is mystically shown that the gentile world with Judea was to be brought forth into the one fellowship of faith through the wave of baptism.
17_marg1732: The divine words, which bring forth the light of wisdom; whence: "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light" etc. Hence Solomon says: "Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light." The candlesticks are twice five, because there are five volumes of the lawgiver, in which also the whole series of the old Testament [and] the five ages of the world are comprised. Five are placed on the right and five on the left, when after the Lord's incarnation the same Scripture is committed to both peoples, or is shown to be full of gospel figures, which was once thought to be understood only according to the letter.
17_interl2256: in Kings in the singular number: "And the table of gold, upon which the loaves of proposition should be set"
17_marg1733: It is credible that these tables were made both for the loaves of proposition and for carrying the vessels of the Lord. Or he put the plural number for the singular in the usual way, as in Jesus Nave: "But the children of Israel transgressed the commandment, and took to their own use of the anathema", though Achor alone did this. Or because the loaves of proposition used to be baked before the sabbath, so as to be set forth at once on the sabbath on the table of proposition. Yet it could be that the new loaves, newly baked, were laid on those tables and kept there covered that night, until early in the morning, the old ones being taken away, they were set warm upon the table of proposition. But as the one table laden with twelve loaves signifies the unanimous concord of all Scripture fortified by apostolic authority, so the ten golden tables [signify] the words of the divine law and of the prophets, which bring forth to us as loaves the refreshment of the word of God, as they set forth the examples of the faithful placed as it were upon them, the brightness and miracles of the vessels of God.
17_marg1734: The golden table is sacred Scripture, fruitful [so the edition: 'secunda'] with the brightness of spiritual knowledge; of which the Psalm says: "Thou hast prepared a table before me, against them that afflict me." The loaves of proposition are the holy teachers, whose works are set before us as saving breasts for examples of life.
17_marg1735: The court of the priests expresses in the Church the life of the perfect, who by excellence of virtues draw near to the Lord and are wont to show others the way by word and work. For a priest [sacerdos] is so called because he gives sacred guidance [sacrum ducatum] to the lesser. By this name not only bishops or presbyters, but all who excel in loftiness of life and saving doctrine are wont to be called: those, namely, who profit not themselves only but many, who, presenting their bodies "a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God", exercise the priestly ministry; to whom it is said through Peter: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc.
17_marg1736: In Kings thus: "And king Solomon built the inner court with three rows of polished stones, and one row of cedar beams." He speaks briefly of the inner court, of the outer he seems to be wholly silent. But in the Words of the days mention is made of both. The inner court, then, which is called that of the priests because the priests and Levites ministered in it, surrounded the temple on every side; but on the east, where the entrance of the temple was, it was set much further from the temple, because there, that is, in front of the temple, the ministries of the sacred rites were done. There [was] the brazen altar for offering victims; there the ten lavers for washing them; there the brazen sea for washing the hands and feet of the priests when they entered to minister. And this court had three cubits of height, according to Josephus, so as to keep others from the entrance of the temple and signify that these things were lawful for the priests alone. It had a gate on the eastern side, up to which the people brought victims and sacrifices, to be received thence by the priests and carried to the altar. What is said less fully here of the courts or porches we have set out more fully in the book of Kings, according to Bede.
17_marg1737: Which was outside the court of the priests, into which all the people flocked to pray or to hear the word. This signifies in the Church the life and morals of the carnal, to whom it is said: "I could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal" etc.
17_marg1738: And a hall etc. Well are the carnal signified by the great hall, because the number of such in the Church is much greater than that of the perfect. But as much as they surpass in number, so much they fall short in merit. Hence this great hall, though it holds very many, does not admit them to the office of the altar, nor even into the court of the priests itself; because the carnal and weak, though for the merit of chaste faith and piety they belong to the lot of the elect, are yet far from those who say: "I dare not to speak of any of those things which Christ worketh not by me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed."
17_interl2258: this signifies the life and morals of the carnal, to whom it is said: "I could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal" etc.
17_marg1739: AND DOORS IN THE HALL etc. These signify that the entrance of faith is prepared by the word of preaching, so that those who come may learn how they ought to enter the Church of God through faith in Christ or the saving sacraments, and, after they have entered, how religiously they ought to live.
17_interl2260: for receiving the ashes of the altar of holocaust
17_marg1740: The caldrons receive the sacred ashes when the faithful with devout mind turn over the examples and sacraments of the Lord's passion for their own keeping, or look diligently on the end of the just, who after great struggles endured rejoice without end in the prize received; so that, having considered the virtues of their elders, they too may be made great. Whence: "Considering the end of their conversation, follow their faith."
17_interl2261: fleshhooks, by which the flesh of the victims was drawn from the caldrons and offered for men to eat
17_marg1741: The fleshhooks signify the preachers, who refresh the souls of the faithful with the word of God, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, but ministering to the carnal the milk of simple doctrine; and those who wish to know the sacraments of Christ in summary and take them up for imitation are, as carnal men, filled with the flesh of the saving victim. And because it belongs to teachers to divide to each what is fitting, rightly are fleshhooks made for the priests, by which they may arrange the flesh of the victims as is fitting, and bring some to clean men, and leave others to be consumed by the fires of the altar; for some things are revealed to our lowliness for refreshment, some are open only to the knowledge of the Holy Spirit.
17_marg1742: Some things in Paralipomenon which have been expounded in Kings we pass over. Some we have not found expounded, and we do not wish to exceed the custom of our littleness. For nowhere have we expounded anything of ourselves.
17_marg1743: AND BOWLS etc. The bowls signify the broader and more open speech of holy doctrine, which gives a draught of wisdom to those who thirst devoutly, and grants fitting refreshment to those who labour devoutly through the ministry of the preachers, that they may come to the fountain of eternal life, from which those who drink "shall not thirst for ever".
17_interl2267: of these it has been treated above
17_interl2268: that is, as a father to be revered
17_marg1744: IN THE COUNTRY NEAR THE JORDAN etc. The Jordan, in which Christ was baptized, who, dipped in its waves, turned for us the element of waters into the washing away of sins. And because every baptism of the faithful, by which we are consecrated to the Lord, is celebrated after the example of that baptism, rightly were the vessels of the house of the Lord made in the country of the Jordan. For we cannot be made vessels of election otherwise than by looking to his baptism and striving to be washed in the life-giving river. And it is to be noted that he says the vessels were made not only in the country of the Jordan but in its plain country, signifying the multiplication of the faithful, which was to be not only in Judea but in the breadth of the nations; whence: "The plains shall be joyful, and all that are in them." And elsewhere: "We have heard of it in Ephrata: we have found it in the fields of the wood." The king therefore cast the vessels of the house of the Lord in the plain country of the Jordan, because the Lord filled the whole breadth of the world with the baptism of salvation, from which he might make vessels of mercy.
17_marg1745: The clay ground, from which the moulds were made for casting the vessels, signifies sacred Scripture, from which we receive the rule of living well. For as clay hardened by fire shows the form of the Lord's vessel, how great and of what kind they ought to be made, so Scripture shows us the rule of justice which we are to follow, and the examples of the saints, who stood unconquered in all things in the fire of tribulation, so that we may desire to be precious vessels in the house of the Lord. And the brass melted by fire enters the moulds of clay so that a vessel fit for heavenly ministries may be made, when we, softened [unclear in the edition: "salubriter humilitati"] and by the flame of divine charity or of human adversity, enter the way of the fathers by working well, that by running well we may come to their rewards. For it is not always necessary for us to be confined by the rules of working well; but when good work is completed, the palm of blessed reward is to be hoped for. Because the vessels were not always kept shut in the moulds of clay; when they had come to perfection, the enclosures of the moulds being broken, they were brought out into the light and arranged in the temple of the Lord, each in its place. Not that the works of the saints will perish, but when they have received the crown of justice, the offices of laborious working will cease.
17_marg1746: He dictated what Hiram completed by the work itself. But allegorically our Redeemer prepares the adornment of the Church in the holy preachers and all the faithful, and effects the works of the virtues, he who says: "Without me you can do nothing"; and elsewhere: "Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above" etc.
17_interl2269: that is, ten, of which it has been said above
17_interl2270: this too has been expounded above
17_marg1747: The hearts of the perfect, shining with the light of inward charity and chastity, whose loftiness the place of the altar also signifies. For it stood before the door of the Holy of holies, as we read in the making of the tabernacle; on it neither the blood of victims nor libations but only incense was burned, the upper part of which, rising, covered the ark and filled the oracle with an odour of sweetness. In which the saints are figured, who, while neglecting the desires of temporal things they seek heavenly things with their whole intent, are as it were placed within, near the oracle, and not far removed from the veil by which the temple and the Holy of holies are divided; because only in body do they dwell on earth, but with their whole mind are in heaven. And the smoke of the incense rises from this altar within the Holy of holies, where the ark is laid up, so that the prayers of the saints, kindled by the flame of charity, may reach heaven, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God. For on this altar not the blood of victims but only incense is burned, because such men have not works of flesh and blood to slay to the Lord on the altar of the heart, but offer vows of tears and prayers out of desire for the heavenly kingdom.
17_interl2272: because most bright with the light of true wisdom
17_interl2273: shapes of lilies on the candlestick, upon which the lamps were set
17_interl2274: snuffers, with which the wicks of the candlestick were snuffed, that, renewed, they might shine better
17_marg1748: The tongs for the use of the altar were made of brass. But these too, with which the lamps were cleaned, signify the interpretation of the spiritual sense through the offices of the teachers. For, transferring the very words of the sacred speech from history to allegory, from shadow to truth, they multiply as it were the light of knowledge in the Church, placed upon the mystical candlestick.
17_interl2275: the vessels in which the incense was made fragrant are the hearts of the teachers, in which prayer is pure and sweetly burning; whence: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight"
17_interl2277: in Kings thus: "And the hinges of the doors of the inner house of the holy of holies, and of the doors of the house of the temple, were of gold"
17_interl2278: the angelic ministries which open to us, when we go forth from the body, the entrance of heavenly life
17_marg1749: These are the teachers and priests who, by instructing, baptizing and giving communion of the mysteries of the body and blood of the Lord, open to us the first thresholds of the Church.
17_marg1750: When the true peacemaker on the last day glorifies all the elect with the immortality of the resurrection. But as long as the state of this world goes on, Solomon does the work of the house of the Lord but does not finish it; because the Lord inspires and helps the hearts of the elect to do good, yet grants to none to be without sin, which he reserves for the faithful in the future. But he finishes all the work of his temple and makes it ready for dedication when he leads the elect, taken from this life, to the eternal kingdom. Hence it is built in seven years, and dedicated finished in the eighth. For in seven days all time revolves; the eighth is the day of judgment and resurrection, to which what follows fits.
17_interl2282: the eloquent, whom Christ by the grace of his Spirit shapes for speaking the gospel
17_interl2283: those endowed with natural genius, whom, filled with his Spirit, he enlightens to consider the wonderful things in his law
17_interl2284: all the sons of the Church, whom the grace of the Holy Spirit inflames to love and seek the gifts of everlasting salvation
17_marg1751: THE LEVITES CARRIED THE ARK etc. This is done when Christ, the universal judgment being finished, brings the company of teachers and other faithful into the joy of the kingdom. And he lays up the vessels of divers kinds, silver or gold, in the treasuries of the house of the Lord, when those who have merited to enjoy the multitude of his sweetness "he hides in the secret of his face from the disturbance of men". And fitly there are many treasuries in which the vessels of love are laid up, but one house of the Lord in which the treasuries are; because there is one Church in which all the elect are contained, though differing in merits, and one heavenly homeland promised to all, though "star differeth from star in glory". Whence: "In my Father's house there are many mansions." Solomon therefore made one house of the Lord, but prepared in it many treasuries, hallowed by one blessing only, to receive vessels of divers kinds; because the Father's house is one, but in it are many mansions for receiving all those who fear and love him: "The Lord hath blessed the little with the great."
17_interl2285: the ark brought into the Holy of holies signifies the humanity of Christ assumed and led within the veil of the heavenly palace
17_interl2286: these are the preachers of the word, through whom he became known to the world
17_marg1752: AND THE STAVES WITH WHICH etc. It is to be noted that although the ends of the staves were seen before the oracle by those who came nearer and looked diligently, yet it could not be that those ends themselves stood out before the oracle; because it was necessary that, the oracle being shut and the veil hung before the doors, the staves too should be hidden within with the ark and the cherubim; which could not be if the staves, projecting further, did not give room for the doors to be brought forward to shut; whose position Scripture has so diligently set out in a great sacrament. For it is agreed that the outer house of the temple designates the Church on pilgrimage on earth, but the Holy of holies the happiness of the inner homeland.
17_marg1753: The tips of the staves appeared outside before the oracle, not always, but when the doors of the oracle were opened; and not to all, but to those who, coming nearer, looked more attentively at what was within. But what the ark itself was like and how it was placed was permitted to be seen only by those who entered the oracle; because none of the saints in this life, though he raise himself much in loftiness of mind, but only the citizens of that homeland fully behold the glory of their Redeemer. But the staves were hidden with the ark in the oracle, because all the perfect who have gone before us are hidden in the secret of God's face from the disturbance of men. Yet the tips of the staves are seen, when the oracle is open, by those who draw near, when divine grace has given to the more perfect, who purify the oracle of their heart with their whole intent, something inward of the joy of the heavenly citizens to contemplate. Which contemplation is not granted to those who have withdrawn a little further; for the more they remain outside with wandering mind, the less they see the inward joys.
17_marg1754: He shows generally that in the ark there was nothing contrary to the law of the Lord contained in the two tables, but that only those things were laid up there which according to the commandments of the law were made typically for the worship of the one God and the commendation of our faith; so that "the shadow of things to come" might in all things bear witness to the truth to come, and might receive its end when that appeared in the world. And there was in the ark, according to Paul, a golden pot that had manna, because in the man Christ "dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally". There was also the rod of Aaron, which, cut off, had flowered again, because all power of judging belongs to him whose judgment seemed to be taken away in the humility of the passion. There were also the tables of the Testament, because in him are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The staves also by which it was carried cleaved to it, because the teachers who once laboured in the word of Christ now rejoice in the glory of Christ by present vision. Whence: "I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ."
17_interl2287: for the twenty-four courses had not yet cast lots who should minister first or second or third, but all, sanctified, served alike
17_marg1755: By the robes of fine linen is designated bodily chastity, white with cleanness; with this all are clothed who stand in the office of God and sound his praises with mouth, morals and act. For the cymbals signify the confession of the mouth; the psalteries, mortality [so the edition]; the harps, instructed with twenty-four strings, that is, with the prophetic and apostolic teachings, the mortification of the flesh and the vigour of good action.
17_interl2288: because by the altar of faith they awaited the rising of the eternal light
17_marg1756: Or the teachers, that is, expressed by the hundred and twenty, because the lawgiver completed the sum of his years in this number, and on the day of Pentecost believers in the same number received the grace of the Spirit the Paraclete.
17_marg1757: While all the priests and Levites sang the praise of God in the temple with instruments of divers kinds, the priests could not stand and minister because of the cloud, or according to Kings because of the mist; because when Christ and the apostles preached his gospel, the proud high priests of the Jews, as their deserts required, while they hear the divine mysteries in parables, cannot minister, as priests of the house of the Lord, because of the cloud. They too, in the old Testament, while they disdain to search out the mystical senses covered by the veil of the letter, lose the ministry due to their faith because of the cloud. To them too that was cloudy which the Lord said openly of himself: "I and the Father are one", and that: "Before Abraham was made, I am." But because the darkness of unbelief had covered the minds of the hearers, the cloud, lying between, had as it were hidden the rays of the sun. For the cloud signifies darkness of understanding. This filled the synagogue, that is, the house of God, and the priests could not minister because of the cloud, because while they were darkened by their unbelief from the understanding of the incarnation of God, they lost the ministry of the true priesthood.
17_marg1758: FOR THE GLORY HAD FILLED etc. Because the mysteries which lay hid under the veil were opened by the coming of Christ to those who believed and received them worthily. But for the rest, who would not come to the faith, the former blindness remained. Whence: "To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God" etc.
17_marg1759: Hence Job: "The clouds are his covert." And the Psalmist: "Darkness was under his feet", and: "He made darkness his covert." The covert of the Lord is sacred Scripture, which bears heavenly sacraments under parables and figures. Whence: "I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones."
17_interl2292: the solidity of true humility, which Christ taught by word and showed by example
17_interl2293: because, according to the tradition of the law, he commends to us that we should have the length of patience and the breadth of love
17_interl2294: because he teaches us to hold the confession of the holy Trinity in faith, hope and charity, and to persist firmly in it by working well
17_interl2295: or and that thou mayest hear
17_interl2300: because the majesty had filled the temple of the Lord
17_interl2303: he cleansed it with his blood
17_marg1760: HE DEDICATED [so the edition: 'DEDICAVI'] THE HOUSE etc. Christ cleansed it with his blood, and sanctified it with spiritual grace, and multiplied it with divers gifts of virtues. And the children of Israel dedicate it, because every faithful man, according to the gift bestowed on him by God, converts and advances his neighbours by word and example to better and more perfect things.
17_marg1761: Because Christ accomplishes in the Church the things which could not be accomplished in the law because of its weakness. For it is the court of the house of the Lord, through which entrance lies open into the heavenly Jerusalem. Because, then, holocausts and sacrifices could not be offered on the altar of the old Testament, since all things were done there in figure, our king and priest set up a new altar of faith in the Church, on which they daily offer fat holocausts and sacrifices acceptable to God. Whence: "The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: and there is the way by which I will shew him" etc.
17_interl2306: that is, the northern quarter of the land of promise
17_marg1762: AND SOLOMON KEPT etc. RABANUS. I do not think anything else is to be understood here than that, the seven days of the dedication of the temple being completed, the days of the Feast of Tabernacles followed, because according to the law they began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and ended on the twenty-second. Both festivals, then, having been duly carried out, and the eighth day of Tabernacles finished, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, rejoicing and glad for the good which the Lord had done to David and to Solomon and to Israel his people.
17_marg1763: Solomon, the work of the temple being completed, held a solemn festival, and a multitude of people with him from the entering in of Emath to the torrent of Egypt; this is the inward joy of the saints which they have for ever with the true peacemaker. For Emath is interpreted 'truth of the Lord'. And by the brook or torrent of Egypt we understand temporal death, which no one in Egypt, that is, in the darkness of this world, can escape. Whence: "Who is the man that shall live, and not see death?" Of Christ also it is said: "He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head." All Israel, then, from the brook of Egypt to Emath, keep a solemn feast with Solomon, because the saints after the end of the present life enjoy eternal joys with Christ. They celebrate the festival for twice seven days, because the elect, enlightened by the grace of the sevenfold Holy Spirit, rejoice in this life, which runs by the number seven, in hope, and in the sabbath, that is, the future rest of souls, in reality, by the receiving of the truth itself.

17_marg1764: SO ON THE DAY etc. That is, after the eighth day of the solemnity of Tabernacles, as is contained in Kings. And it signifies that after the end of that life, and after the sabbath rest of the holy souls in which they rest before the judgment, in the eighth age, that is, on the day of resurrection, the saints will receive immortal bodies and be placed in the heavenly mansions according to the quality of their merits, where they will always rejoice, praising God in all the good things which the Father has conferred in Christ on the Christian people.
17_marg1765: HIRAM HAD GIVEN. That is, had given back; because when Solomon had given them, they did not please him. Therefore Solomon assigned them to his own uses.
17_interl2312: which in Hebrew is called Thamar
17_marg1766: BETHORON THE UPPER AND THE NETHER etc. It is a city as far as which Jesus [Josue] pursued the enemy kings, in the tribe of Ephraim etc., as far as: and another Bethoron the nether, given to the Levites for a possession.

17_marg1767: AND ALL THE STRONGEST CITIES etc. That is, Ezer, Mageddo, Gazer and Mello, which all show the beauty of the Church, because the true Solomon prepared it for himself for praise and joy in the gladness of his kingdom. And Mello is interpreted 'fulfilment', Ezer 'separated and sanctified', Mageddo 'his upper chamber', Gazer 'cutting off' or 'division', Bethoron 'house of mountains', Balaath 'ascending'. And holy Church is the city of the living God, where the will of God is daily fulfilled, and, separated from all error of unbelievers, it is sanctified by faith and good work. There is the refreshment of the virtues. It discerns clean and unclean, and vice from virtue; and it is the house of mountains, that is, the dwelling of the saints, and with the fruit of justice, "like a palm tree flourishing", it "goes from virtue to virtue, to see the God of gods in Sion". Solomon fortified all his villages, because Christ so fortifies the companies of his faithful with the protection of his grace that they can resist their spiritual enemies. In Libanus: that is, in the temple, which was clothed with the beauty of cedars, whence Zacharias: "Open thy gates, O Libanus"; or in the royal buildings, which were made of the wood of Libanus.

17_marg1768: The hundred, which in counting on the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, signifies eternal life. The fifty signifies the remission of sins, eternal rest and the grace of the Holy Spirit; because in the Psalm of the same number penance, confession and the remission of sins are described, and by the jubilee the future rest; and by Pentecost, in the coming of the Holy Spirit, the sevenfold grace is expressed.
17_marg1769: Because from both peoples he chose rulers of the Church who, enlightened by spiritual grace and fully taught, should teach by their example the remission of sins and the life of eternal salvation, and perpetual blessedness to be sought.

17_marg1770: HOLOCAUSTS TO THE LORD. A holocaust is called 'wholly burnt'. This is burnt on the altar when in the heart of each of the elect, who has vowed himself wholly, that is, in flesh and heart, to God, good work is kindled with the glowing fire of charity.

17_marg1771: ACCORDING TO THE RITE OF EVERY DAY etc. He orders all things in the Church according to what befits each time, that each order, performing its office, may minister worthily.
17_marg1772: It is said to be an island not far from Ailath in the Red Sea, where the fleet of Josaphat perished.
17_marg1773: The fleet which Solomon made in Asiongaber, which is interpreted 'hastening' or 'strong' or 'manfully', is understood as the Church of the faithful, which, set in the sea of this world, strives to acquire the treasures of wisdom and knowledge and the riches of the virtues; where Hiram's servants, sailors and skilled in the sea, are with Solomon's servants, because gentiles learned in the wisdom of the world are joined in the unity of faith with those skilled in the law of Moses. These our Solomon sends to Ophir, which is interpreted 'weakening', to bring gold from there, when they labour to seek a precious sense in the lowliness of the letter; and, having received the sum of four hundred and fifty talents of gold, they bring it to the king, when through the grace of the Holy Spirit they find in the divine books the precious sense of history, allegory, tropology and anagogy, and render it [unclear in the edition: "eum sapientie et consilio divina ascribentes"].
17_marg1774: Ophir, the name of a province, called after one of the descendants of Heber, of whose stock those who came, Josephus relates, dwelt from the river Cophen as far as the region of India which is called Geria.
17_interl2337: a royal city of Ethiopia, which Josephus relates was surnamed Meroe by king Cambyses from the name of his sister
17_marg1775: The queen of the south, who, roused from the furthest ends [of the earth], came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, figured the Church of the gentiles that was to come to Christ, which, "surrounded with variety in gilded clothing, forgetting her people and her father's house", was barbarian in race, not in mind, because she desired to become a fellow citizen of the saints. Whence: "The queen of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation."
17_marg1776: Saba is interpreted 'conversion' or 'captivity', because the Church, converted to the faith of Christ, merited to belong to the lot of his captivity, of which it is said: "Ascending on high, he led captivity captive." She brought to the true Solomon on camels spices, gold and precious stones, when she brought to the faith of Christ gentiles misshapen by the strength of their sins, but flourishing in genius and study, and apt, as the preachers dispensed it, to receive the brightness of wisdom and the precious gems of the virtues; with which she honoured our Solomon with solemn worship, nay, honoured by him, received a greater grace of spiritual gift. Whence in what follows: King Solomon gave the queen of Saba all that she desired etc. For in the present he confers the grace of the Holy Spirit and wisdom and virtues; in the future, in the sight of his glory, he will bestow eternal life.

Hence also, in wonder, she bursts out in his praise, saying: Blessed are thy men etc.

17_marg1778: OF THE THYINE TREES. Christ sets the precious trees, that is, the holy teachers, the greenness of whose faith never withers, nor do the leaves of their words fall, but "they bring forth the fruit of good works in their seasons", for the defence of the house of the Lord and of the royal house, that is, for the strengthening of the Church, that, walled about on every side by their teachings and examples, it may not feel ruin. These are said to be made as harps and lyres for praising the Lord, because "whatsoever they shall do shall prosper", and they proclaim the praise of the Lord in prosperity and adversity with heart and mouth and work, and do all things to the glory of God, and day and night do not cease to praise the name of the Lord.
17_interl2349: in the six, the perfection of the gifts which are to be brought by us to our king
17_marg1779: Six multiplied by six makes sixty [so the edition]. A hundred also, taken six times, gives a hundred and six [so the edition]. The ten signifies the perfection of the commandments, the hundred the reward of eternal blessedness. For the king desires our perfection, that he may have those to whom he may render a perfect reward. Whence: "Be you perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect"; "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments." And after a little: "If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell what thou hast" etc.; "and every one that hath left house etc. shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting."
17_marg1780: Divers nations and merchants and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the lands offer gold and silver to Solomon, because every nation and every person vies, according to its strength, to offer our peacemaker the gift of right faith, purity of sense, fulness of holy confession, brightness of eloquence. Whence: "The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents" etc., "and all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him."
17_marg1781: Because the fathers of both Testaments, perfect in doctrine and working, proved by work whatever they taught by word.
17_marg1782: This is the armour of God, by which we stand against the snares of the devil; which the holy preachers have, who guard the house of God and keep watch at its door lest the ancient enemy steal in. Whence: "Threescore valiant ones surround the bed of Solomon."
17_marg1783: It signifies perfect faith in the confession of the holy Trinity. Well do the guards of the house of God carry golden spears and shields, because the preachers, who are the guards of the Church, shining with the brightness of wisdom, pierce the enemies with the darts of words, and "with the shield of faith extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one".
17_interl2351: that is, the Church, where the spiritual armour is laid up, by which the faithful are protected and the enemies driven back

17_marg1784: That is, the Church, in which the just peacemaker reigns and judges, because "the soul of the just is the seat of God".

17_marg1785: In the six [is] the perfection of good works. For in six days God made the world, and six is the first perfect number. And by good and perfect works one ascends to heaven.
17_marg1786: [It signifies] the saints shining with the splendour of the virtues, in whom God dwells. By the footstool can also be marked those who are weak in the body of Christ, as penitents, or those who will be converted last, namely near the end of the world, who yet are golden, refined and proved in the fire of the tribulations of that time.
17_interl2356: the fathers of both Testaments, strong in mind, ruling themselves and others
17_marg1787: Because the holy fathers attributed whatever good they did in the gospel not to themselves but to God. Whence: "Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory."
17_marg1788: In Kings thus: "And two hands on either side holding the seat." These are the comforts of divine grace, which advance the Church to the heavenly kingdom. Or this is designated by the two, because in both Testaments this is most commended: that nothing good can be accomplished except by divine help. Whence: "Without me you can do nothing."
17_interl2357: the preachers following the apostolic teaching
17_marg1789: Because they strive by teaching and example that the labour of the unwise may not totter in working, but may keep uprightness strongly in the progress of the virtues.
17_marg1790: Because of the Church it is written: "Strength and beauty are her clothing" etc., and: "Many daughters have gathered together riches: thou hast surpassed them all."
17_marg1791: The souls of the saints, which serve the will of God, shining with the splendour of wisdom and charity, contain the drink of living water, "which becomes in them a fountain of water springing up into life everlasting".
17_marg1792: The word of God is not in speech but in power, as "in the preaching of the gospel, not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in shewing of the Spirit and power".
17_marg1793: FOR THE KING'S SHIPS WENT WITH THE SERVANTS etc. Christ sends into the world the apostles, teachers of the gospel, whom he chose from the Jews, together with the preachers chosen from the gentiles, with a threefold confession but one faith, that in those who believe they may bring him the gold of wisdom, the silver of eloquence and the ivory of chastity. And the ape is a clever animal and an imitator of man, and can signify the philosophers, who sometimes change the senses of true wisdom and set forth the acts of moral life in their disciplines. The peacock, which shows its praised feathers, signifies those who for the praises of men display the appearances of various virtues; but, instructed by the teaching of the preachers, they learn to do good in view of God alone, and are fitted for the delights of the eternal king.
17_interl2358: "For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord?" etc.
17_interl2359: "Great and terrible above all them that are about him"
17_interl2360: "My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek." And elsewhere: "As the hart panteth after the fountains of water, so my soul panteth after thee, O God"
17_marg1794: The forty signifies the times of the ancient law. For Moses, about to receive the law, fasted forty days, and the people instructed by him went round the desert forty years. And the six [so the edition: 'senarius'] signifies the present time, in which the apostolic doctrine of the New Testament nourishes the people. Well then are the horses of Solomon placed in the stalls numbered by forty, because by the hardness of the old law the insolence of the former people was restrained. And the twelve signifies the present time, in which apostolic authority nourishes the people of the gentiles with the doctrine of the new Testament.
17_interl2361: in the keeping of the disciplines
17_marg1795: IN JERUSALEM: in the vision of peace. The distance of the places shows a distinction of dispositions. For those who are in the cities of the chariots signify those who are taught in the various disciplines of the Church by spiritual masters. But others, already taught and fitted for the use of the heavenly king, merit to have his presence. Whence: "The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands" etc. And elsewhere: "Who wilt ride upon thy horses: and thy riding is salvation."
17_interl2362: "And he shall rule from sea to sea" etc.
17_interl2363: that is, over all who exercise the power of right rule
17_marg1796: Of those falling doubly. For Philistiim is interpreted 'double ruin'. This is done when, through the absolution of sins from its beginning in the Jordan of baptism up to the conversion of all nations to the faith of Christ, the grace of [his] power overflows; so that where there was the outflow of carnal desires, there the seed of the virtues may be established, and where the idolatry and shameful conduct of the peoples was a double ruin, there through the confession of right faith and the worship of piety the life of the faithful may rise to the heavenly kingdom. For his power reaches to the borders of Egypt, that is, the darkened minds of unbelievers, which he fills with the light of faith. Whence: "Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down" etc.
17_interl2365: in the silver, the brightness of eloquence and the pleasantness of the Church's doctrine
17_interl2366: of the hardness and insensibility of the gentiles
17_marg1797: The true Solomon gives in the Church plenty of silver as of stones, when he turns the hearts of the gentiles, insensible to the understanding of the true God, who worshipped stones for God, to the meditation of the law and the preaching of the gospel. Of whom it is said: "Let them that make them become like unto them" etc. And elsewhere: "God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham." He gives also a multitude of cedars as of sycamores, because he advanced the barrenness of the gentiles, who would not raise themselves on high, to the fruitfulness of good works and virtues.
17_interl2367: in the cedars, the fineness and fragrance of the virtues
17_marg1798: The cedar is of an incorruptible nature, pleasant in smell, bright in appearance, and when kindled it drives away and kills serpents by its brightness.
17_interl2368: in the sycamores, the vileness and unfruitfulness of unbelievers
17_interl2369: the first, which he did before he transgressed, such as the building of the temple and the various offering of sacrifices
17_marg1799: Those which he did after he transgressed the law of God, when his foreign wives drew him even to idolatry. Many indeed, like Solomon, begin well and end badly; and no one ought to be called blessed before his death and last funeral rites.
